newsitem.title: CHINA: China not to raise power prices in short term.
newsitem.headline: China not to raise power prices in short term.

text.p: China will implement no large increase in electricity prices in the short term, the Economic Information Daily quoted Minister of Power Industry Shi Dazhen as saying.
Some people have voiced fears that electricity prices may rise swiftly after the January establishment of the China State Electricity Co, a power ministry official said.
"This is not going to happen because prices are strictly controlled by the central government," the official said.
The electricity price for private users has doubled in the last 20 years in most cities, but the rise was much lower than inflation in the same period, the Economic Information Daily said.
Currently, the main reason that could prompt the government to raise electricity fees would be the higher cost of raw materials, the official said.

The China State Electricity Co now takes responsibility for inter-regional power supplies and has unified management of the national power grid. It is to replace the Ministry of Power Industry in a year or two, the ministry official said.
